summary: Tested the Letters module (/letters) for both reported fixes, on the backend (pytest, 10/10 passed) and the frontend (Playwright). BUG FIX 1 (isolation) works. A general letter issued by Saeed is stored with created_by_faculty_ids=[698e4fb4...a6] (his department resolves to its parent faculty). Saeed and admin can see it. Salim cannot see it in GET /letters?q=, and GET /letters/{id} returns 403 for him. The reverse case also works: Salim's letter is tagged with his faculty and is hidden from Saeed. Admin's general letters still have created_by_faculty_ids=[] and are visible to everyone. Admin still sees all 127 letters. Letters about a specific person still show up through the old scope (a letter about a student in Salim's faculty is visible to Salim). Draft, duplicate, finalize, delete-draft and issue all return 200 for admin, Salim and Saeed, with the correct scope tag. Existing data was not changed by mistake: 0 of the 127 pre-existing letters were tagged by the startup backfill. BUG FIX 2: the PNG live preview shows bold, color and font as typed. When preview-pdf is forced to 500, the fallback now shows real HTML (strong, color rgb(198,40,40), the inline font-family span), not plain text. Templates keep their formatting through create -> 'استخدام' (Saeed) or the dropdown (admin) -> editor -> edit modal -> save -> reload. NEW ROOT CAUSE FOUND for 'templates lose their formatting': a global CSS rule in app/_layout.tsx forces Cairo on every element with !important. As a result, the font chosen in StatementBodyEditor (and in the HTML fallback preview) is never displayed. The inline font-family:Tajawal/Almarai/Amiri is in the HTML, but the computed font is always Cairo. To the user, the template or letter looks like it went back to plain formatting, even though the data and the PDF are correct. All four admin tabs render fine.

minor.issue: _finalize_fields uses the scope of the user who finalizes, not the draft author's. When admin finalizes a draft created by Saeed, created_by_faculty_ids is overwritten from [Saeed's faculty] to [], so the general letter becomes visible to all deans and department heads (reproduced: Salim could see it). Suggested fix: in finalize_draft, keep ex.get('created_by_faculty_ids') if it is not empty, or compute the scope from the draft's created_by user.

has_own_academic_scope() is true for ANY role that has faculty_id or department_id (for example employees like view_curr_user, or university_president if a faculty is set), not only dean/department_head. This widens isolation beyond the intended roles. No such user currently has issue_letters, so there is no impact today. Consider limiting it to role in {dean, department_head}.

On every startup it re-checks all letters with an empty tag and tags them with the issuer's CURRENT scope. If an unscoped issuer is given a faculty later, their old university-wide letters will be isolated retroactively. Low risk. Consider adding a one-time migration flag.

ui_bugs.issue: Font choices are never displayed in the UI. /app/frontend/app/_layout.tsx line ~40 injects `* { font-family: 'Cairo', ... !important }`, which overrides the inline style font-family set by the Tiptap FontFamily extension. Verified: span inline='Tajawal' but computed='Cairo, Ionicons...'. The same happens for Almarai and Amiri, and the editor root's own font-family:Amiri also shows as Cairo. Color, bold, underline and size display correctly. This most likely explains the user's complaint that 'templates do not keep their formatting'. Fix: add more specific !important overrides in the StatementBodyEditor <style>, e.g. `.stmt-tiptap .tiptap{font-family:Amiri,serif !important}` plus `.stmt-tiptap [style*="font-family: Tajawal"]{font-family:Tajawal !important}` for each of the 5 fonts (or exclude .stmt-tiptap and the preview container from the global * rule with :not()). Apply the same to the letters.tsx fallback preview div (give it a class).

action_items: HIGH: Fix the global `* {font-family: Cairo !important}` override (app/_layout.tsx) so the 5 fonts chosen in StatementBodyEditor and the HTML fallback preview actually display. Add scoped !important rules in the StatementBodyEditor style block.
MEDIUM: finalize_draft should keep the draft author's created_by_faculty_ids, not take the finalizer's (an admin finalizing a dept-head draft currently removes the isolation).
LOW: Limit _isolation_scope's academic fallback to dean/department_head roles. Consider a one-time flag for backfill_letters_isolation_scope.
critical_code_review_comments: Only server.py:19326 still uses hr_scope_isolation_faculty_ids (other modules: fee receipts/reports). Its behavior is unchanged because _isolation_scope wraps it and does not modify it. No regression there.
letters.py _visible_filter computes fac_scope only if the user has HR_PERMS or issue_letters. Users who can view letters without issue_letters (if any) skip isolation. Accepted as before.
StatementBodyEditor color buttons had no data-testid. I added data-testid={`${testID}-color-${hex}`} (test-only change, no behavior change).

Testing consumed about 8 official serial numbers in the default numbering series (letters issued and finalized, then hard-deleted by id), so there is a gap in the 26/خ sequence (~141-148). The issued test letters were deleted from db.letters by their ids.

success_rate.backend: 100% (10/10 pytest; 1 minor edge-case bug found separately)
success_rate.frontend: 85% (all flows work; font-family not visible in editor or fallback)

rca of the issue: Formatting complaint: the stored HTML (template/letter body) and the ReportLab PDF keep all formatting. The visual loss of formatting comes from the global CSS rule `* { font-family: 'Cairo', ... !important }` in app/_layout.tsx, which beats Tiptap's inline style="font-family: X". Every font choice therefore looks like Cairo in the editor and in the fallback preview, so templates look 'reset'. Repro: /letters -> type text -> select all -> choose تجوّل -> getComputedStyle shows Cairo. Mitigation: scoped !important CSS overrides per font inside .stmt-tiptap and the fallback container. Isolation edge case: finalize_draft calls _finalize_fields(current_user), which recomputes created_by_faculty_ids from the finalizer. Repro: Saeed saves a draft, admin finalizes it, the tag becomes [], and Salim can see it.
